name: Arcos
evidence: Headline: Munich-based Arcos raises €5.5 million to build and operate civil safety infrastructure across Europe

Summary: Arcos, a Munich-based startup that builds and operates civil security infrastructure, has closed a €5.5 million Seed funding round. The company launched publicly today. The round was led by High-Tech Gründerfonds (HTGF), with participation from Bayern Kapital, Pact, Haufe, Robin Capital, and strategic business angels. “Europe has understood that its safety is its own responsibility, […] The post…
Headline: Arcos secures €5.5M to protect critical infrastructure from physical threats

assessment.whatTheyDo: Builds and operates a proprietary alarm-monitoring, video and signal-processing platform (Trident) plus its own control centers, for security monitoring of critical infrastructure, commercial sites and homes in Europe.
concerns: Headquartered in Munich, Germany, and all listed roles are in Munich. This is materially harder for a US-based candidate (visa, relocation, time zone) and there is no sign of US or remote hiring.
Physical security and alarm monitoring, not cyber or software-security. It fits the 'Cybersecurity and privacy engineering' theme only loosely.
Sits near the defense/civil-security boundary. The company positions itself around sabotage protection and European sovereignty, but describes its work as civil, not weapons systems.
Operating control centers is human-staffed and services-heavy. The business may look more like a security services company than a pure software company, and margins and scalability are unclear.
Founder technical backgrounds are not disclosed in any source I found, so the 'strong technical founders' criterion can't be verified.
No named customers, and no team size or revenue figures published.
Only two engineering roles are open (Forward Deployed Engineer, Member of Technical Staff (Platform)), with no seniority stated.
assessment.rationale: The product looks real: it is shipped, VdS 3534 certified, and the company has raised a sensible €5.5M seed. It is an operations-heavy physical-security business, though, and only loosely matches the person's interest themes. It is also Munich-only, which the person's geography preference penalises. The score reflects the location and theme mismatch and is not a judgment that the company is weak.
assessment.summary: Arcos is a Munich startup, about a year old, founded by Louis Wübben and Moritz Steigerwald. It builds Trident, a unified platform for alarm, video and emergency-call signals, and runs its own control centers for critical infrastructure and commercial and residential customers. A €5.5M seed led by HTGF suggests credible backing, but the Munich-only hiring and physical-security focus make it a weak fit for a US-based engineer.
assessment.product: Trident, a proprietary software platform that unifies signals from alarms, video and emergency calls as objects in one model, combined with Arcos-operated control centers. It is built for European critical infrastructure (railway stations, substations, data centers), commercial sites and residential customers, with EU data governance, VdS 3534 certification, and customer data kept separate from AI model training.
assessment.team: Founders and Managing Directors Louis Wübben and Moritz Steigerwald. No press or investor source gave their backgrounds, and no team size is disclosed. The company is about one year old.
assessment.funding: €5.5M Seed announced 2026-09-18, led by High-Tech Gründerfonds (HTGF). Other participants: Bayern Kapital, Pact, Haufe, Robin Capital and unnamed strategic business angels.
redFlags: All open roles are in Munich, with no US or remote hiring evident.
Founder technical depth is unverified.
The business is service- and operations-heavy, with control centers staffed by humans.
No named customers or revenue disclosed.
greenFlags: Product is shipped and certified (VdS 3534).
Builds its own software and operates its own control centers, so engineers sit close to real incidents and product decisions.
Small team, and an engineering platform role titled Member of Technical Staff suggests leverage.
Reasonable seed size (€5.5M) with a shipped product, not an outsized round with nothing built.
Solid institutional backers (HTGF, Bayern Kapital) and a real market driver in European critical-infrastructure security spending.

name: Boxd
evidence: Headline: Boxd raises $2M to build cloud infrastructure for AI coding agents

Summary: Dutchstartup Boxd has raised $2 million in a pre-seed funding round to develop itscloud computing infrastructure for developers and AI coding agents. The roundwas led by BlueYard Capital, with partici...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Boxd builds persistent, forkable KVM virtual machines (custom virtualization) that developers and AI coding agents use as full cloud computers, with live memory forking in under 100-200ms.
matchedInterests: Databases, distributed systems, and cloud infrastructure
Agent frameworks, evaluation, and LLM tooling
concerns: Headquartered in the Netherlands, with roles listed only for Bucharest or Amsterdam. That makes it materially harder for a US-based candidate to join, with visa, relocation and time-zone issues.
Very early: pre-seed, founded in 2026, and no named customers or traction found.
Crowded agent-sandbox market (E2B, Modal, Daytona, Blaxel, Fly.io Machines and others). The moat is mostly technical execution on virtualization and speed.
The only open engineering role found is a full-stack one; the infrastructure role is already filled. There are no senior or staff roles, and no roles for US remote candidates.
I could not verify the founders' prior backgrounds or their depth in systems and virtualization. LinkedIn and Crunchbase pages did not load.
assessment.rationale: The product is real and shipped. It has public pricing, docs and a live site, it is technically deep (KVM VMs, live memory forking, hibernation), and it sits squarely in the cloud infrastructure and agent tooling themes. A $2M pre-seed keeps the team tiny with high engineer leverage. The score is held down by the Europe-only hiring, the crowded sandbox market and founder backgrounds I could not verify.
assessment.summary: Boxd is a 2026 Dutch startup building persistent, forkable cloud VMs for developers and AI coding agents. It raised a $2M pre-seed led by BlueYard Capital in September 2026. The product is live with public pricing and docs, and the technical approach (custom virtualization, sub-100ms live forking) is credible. It is a strong theme match but a hard one for a US-based hire, because roles are in Amsterdam or Bucharest.
assessment.product: Persistent, hardware-isolated KVM Linux VMs (Ubuntu 24.04) that spin up in under 10ms. They support snapshots, live memory forking, hibernation to disk, and pre-authenticated integrations (GitHub, Linear, Slack, OpenAI, Claude). Aimed at coding agents, dev workspaces, preview environments, agent swarms and RL environments. Pricing is usage-based: about €0.049 per vCPU-hour and €0.015 per GiB RAM-hour, with no charge while hibernated.
assessment.team: Founders are Michiel Voortman, Laurentiu Ciobanu and Hidde Kehrer. Press says they are building custom virtualization technology. I could not confirm their prior employers or systems backgrounds. One search snippet says Voortman won a Coinbase AI agent competition and contributed to agent frameworks, which I did not verify. Team size is not stated.
assessment.funding: $2M pre-seed (September 2026) led by BlueYard Capital, with OVNI Capital, Antler, S20 and Script Capital, plus angels from General Intuition and other tech companies. Funds are for growing the team and advancing the custom virtualization tech.
openRoles: Founding Software Engineer, Full-stack (Bucharest or Amsterdam)
redFlags: Europe-based hiring only; no US or remote roles found
No named customers or traction metrics
Founder backgrounds unverified
Crowded agent-sandbox category
greenFlags: Shipped product with public pricing and docs
Technically deep: real KVM VMs, live memory forking, hibernation
Small pre-seed round, so a tiny team with high engineer leverage
Founders offer direct support with no ticket queue, so they are close to users and product
Founding-engineer roles put engineers close to product decisions
Backed by BlueYard, a respected early-stage investor

name: Creem
evidence: Headline: Creem secures €5M to build financial infrastructure for AI-native startups

Summary: Creem, a billing and monetisationplatform for AI-native companies, has raised €5 million in seed funding todevelop its platform and expand its financial and revenue tools for softwarebusinesses. The r...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Creem is a merchant-of-record billing and monetisation platform for AI-native and indie software companies, handling global sales tax and compliance, subscriptions, usage-based pricing, affiliates and revenue splits, with an agent-operable (MCP/CLI/API) layer.
concerns: Headquartered in Tallinn, Estonia. Careers page says it hires engineers, designers and operators in Estonia. Visa, relocation or a time-zone gap makes it materially harder for a US-based candidate, so the score is lowered.
The only role I could confirm is Customer Success Engineer. The Ashby job board (jobs.ashbyhq.com/creem) rendered as 'Armitage Labs' with no listings, so I found no senior or staff engineering roles.
Merchant-of-record billing is a crowded space (Paddle, Stripe/Lemon Squeezy, Polar). The AI-agent angle may be more positioning than moat.
Agent-operated billing and MCP features are mostly roadmap. The €5M is said to fund building them over 12-18 months.
Founders' backgrounds reportedly span payments, embedded finance and crypto. I found no crypto product, but I could not check how much that history matters.
Affiliate management and revenue splits are core features. This is tooling for other businesses, not an affiliate-driven business itself, but it is worth watching.
assessment.rationale: This is a real, revenue-generating fintech/dev-infrastructure company with technical ex-Google/Adyen founders, a tiny team of about 15, and an engineering-led culture. It is a moderate thematic match (fintech is a 0.6-weight interest, and billing is SaaS/dev tooling). The Estonia base, no visible senior engineering roles and a crowded category keep it in the plausible-but-uncertain band.
assessment.summary: Creem is a Tallinn-based billing and merchant-of-record platform for AI-native software companies. It was founded by ex-Google and Adyen engineers and raised a €5M seed led by Inovo VC in September 2026, bringing total funding to about €7M. Press reports over €2M ARR and a team of about 15 that grew from one person in October 2024. It is a credible, small, engineering-led company, but it is Europe-based and competes with well-funded rivals.
assessment.product: A merchant-of-record and billing platform for developers and AI-native software companies selling globally. It covers tax and compliance, subscriptions, usage-based and prepaid credit pricing, affiliate management, revenue splits and conversion analytics. Creem 2.0 adds agent operation through MCP, CLI, API and Slack on a bring-your-own-agent model.
assessment.team: Co-founders Gabriel Ferraz (CEO) and Alec Erasmus, both ex-Google and Adyen. The team was reported at about 15 at the funding announcement. Creem describes itself as 'a small, talented, and engineering-led team'. Finalist candidates get a paid 3-day trial where they are flown in to work on real projects.
assessment.funding: €5M seed led by Inovo VC, with Practica Capital and Antler (existing investors). Angels include Markus Villig (Bolt), Timmu Tõke and Kaspar Tiri (Ready Player Me), Adam Jafer (Voi) and Fryd Wiatrowski (Viktor.com). Pre-seed was about €1.8M in August 2025. Total is about €7M (one outlet says €6.8M).
redFlags: Estonia HQ and Estonia-focused hiring, so a US-based candidate faces visa and time-zone friction.
No senior or staff engineering roles found; the only confirmed opening is customer-success.
Crowded MRP/billing market with well-funded incumbents (Paddle, Stripe).
'AI-native' and agent-operated billing positioning is partly forward-looking marketing.
The mandatory in-person paid trial is a hurdle for someone based in the US.
greenFlags: Real revenue: reported over €2M ARR, more than doubled.
Technically credentialed founders from Google and Adyen.
Small team of about 15, so an engineer would have high leverage and autonomy.
Engineering-led culture, with a paid trial on real work.
The €5M seed is modest and backed by shipped product and revenue, not a large raise with no product.
Fits a real need: compliance-heavy global payments for indie and AI developers.

name: Crusoe
evidence: Headline: Crusoe raises $3.9B to build massive data centers and small modular ‘AI factories’
Summary: The round values the data center giant at $30.9 billion.

assessment.whatTheyDo: Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI infrastructure company that builds and operates data centers (including factory-built modular 'Spark' units) and sells GPU cloud and AI inference compute to customers like Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle.
matchedInterests: Databases, distributed systems, and cloud infrastructure
concerns: The team is far too big for the 'small team, high leverage' preference. Careers aggregators list roughly 1,600 open positions, and I found no exact headcount. A $30.9B valuation means a large, scaling company rather than an early-stage one.

The business is capital-intensive real estate, energy and hardware buildout. Much of the work is construction and operations rather than software, and most hiring is likely data center and go-to-market.
The company started in 2018 as a crypto-mining operation using flared gas. It has since pivoted fully to AI, but it is a legacy tie to an anti-theme.
Revenue is concentrated in a few hyperscale and AI-lab customers, and the business depends on continued AI capex. The reported $13B Jane Street contract is press-reported, not verified.
Equity upside is limited at a $30.9B valuation, roughly triple the $10B mark of October 2025. Engineers would join late-stage and pre-IPO.
The round is far above the $2M–$150M preferred size.
assessment.rationale: This is a substantial, real technical company in cloud and AI infrastructure, which matches two high-weight themes, and it hires senior and principal engineers on backend, streaming and cloud platform work. It is a poor match for the 'early-stage, small team, high leverage' profile, and its round size is 26x the preferred maximum. The score is mid-range: strong theme and evidence, weak stage and leverage fit.
assessment.summary: Crusoe raised a $3.9B Series F at a $30.9B post-money valuation, co-led by Atreides Management, Mubadala Capital and Valor Equity Partners. It runs AI data centers, a GPU cloud and inference services, and is building factories in Colorado and Tulsa to manufacture modular data centers. It is a real, fast-growing infrastructure company with named hyperscale customers, but it is now a large late-stage company rather than a small startup where one engineer moves the needle.
assessment.product: Data center leasing, GPU cloud rental (Crusoe Cloud) and managed AI inference compute, plus modular 'Spark' data centers built in its own factories. Large sites include the Abilene, Texas campus used by OpenAI. Customers are AI labs, hyperscalers and enterprises such as Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle and Jane Street.
assessment.team: Co-founder and CEO Chase Lochmiller leads the company, which was founded in 2018. New board members announced with the round are Thomas Seifert (Cloudflare CFO), Bill Stein (Primary Digital Infrastructure) and JB Straubel (Redwood Materials founder/CEO and Tesla board member). I did not find detailed engineering leadership backgrounds.
assessment.funding: Series F of $3.9B at a $30.9B post-money valuation (Sept 2026), co-led by Atreides Management, Mubadala Capital and Valor Equity Partners. Participants: Founders Fund, GIC, Nvidia, Qatar Investment Authority, Radical Ventures and TPG. The prior Series E was $1.38B at a $10B valuation in Oct 2025.
openRoles: Principal Software Engineer, Crusoe Cloud (San Francisco, CA; listed at $256K–$320K + bonus)
Senior Backend Software Engineer, Cloud Management (Kafka/Flink telemetry streaming)
redFlags: Late-stage, very large company and not a small team.
Crypto-mining origin, now pivoted away.
Capital-intensive and dependent on a few large AI customers and continued AI capex.
Much of the workforce is likely construction, operations and sales rather than software.
greenFlags: Real, revenue-generating product with marquee customers (Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle).
Hiring principal and senior engineers on distributed systems and streaming (Kafka/Flink) and on cloud platform work.
Full-stack control of infrastructure ('electrons to tokens') creates a technical moat in energy, hardware and cloud.
Nvidia and other strong strategic and institutional investors, plus experienced new board members.
US-based, with a San Francisco and Sunnyvale presence in the preferred state (CA).

name: ETFBOOK
evidence: Headline: ETFBOOK raises $13M to expand ETF data and analytics globally

Summary: ETFBOOK (SquaredData AG) has raised $13million in a funding round to expand its ETF data and analytics platform intothe Americas and Asia-Pacific. Expedition Growth Capital led the roundwith participa...

assessment.whatTheyDo: ETFBOOK (SquaredData AG) sells B2B ETF data infrastructure and analytics, via APIs and a web app, that normalizes fragmented ETF data for issuers, market makers and asset managers.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Headquartered in Zurich with the engineering hub in Kraków. Almost all roles are remote within European time zones, so a US-based engineer would face a time-zone and hiring-eligibility gap.
The careers page lists only one US-based role, in New York State, and it is a sales or business role rather than engineering. That is an inference from the role list and not confirmed.
The AI angle (a conversational layer) is only mentioned in press and looks secondary to the data business.

Team of about 30 and 70+ enterprise clients is real but modest, and the founders' technical depth is unverified. The CTO is co-founder Bartłomiej Igła, and the CEO is Pawel Janus, PhD, an analytics background.
Niche B2B finance data market with incumbents (not named in the sources I found), so it may be a slow-moving market rather than a consumer-scale one.
assessment.rationale: This is a real, revenue-generating data platform with 70+ enterprise clients and reported ARR growth above 100% a year. Its data infrastructure and fintech focus fits the interest list. The Europe-centric hiring, the modest team size and the lack of visible US engineering roles pull the score down. Senior engineering roles are being hired (Senior Platform, Data and Full-Stack), which is a positive signal.
assessment.summary: ETFBOOK, run by SquaredData AG, is a Zurich-headquartered ETF data and analytics company founded in 2020, with a delivery hub in Kraków. It raised $13M in September 2026, led by Expedition Growth Capital with existing investor BlackFin Capital Partners, after a €4M round in February 2025. It has about 30 staff and 70+ enterprise clients and says recurring revenue has grown more than 100% a year. It is a credible, shipped product, but the hiring is mostly European and remote.
assessment.product: An ETF-native data intelligence layer for ETF issuers, fund administrators, market makers, authorized participants, asset managers, wealth managers and hedge funds. It has three parts: Data (standardized ETF data via APIs), Analytics (a web application for flows, screening and reports) and Workforce (combining verified ETF data with clients' own or third-party data for ETF data operations). Press says an AI conversational layer is being added.
assessment.team: CEO and co-founder Pawel Janus, PhD, listed as Head of Analytics. Co-founder Bartłomiej Igła, listed as Head of Technology or CTO. Team of 30+ across 10+ countries. I did not find detailed prior employers.
assessment.funding: $13M (September 2026), led by Expedition Growth Capital with existing investor BlackFin Capital Partners. Earlier: €4M (February 2025), per startupticker.ch.
techStack: Data platform / data engineering (specifics not found)
redFlags: Nearly all roles are remote in European time zones, so a US-based candidate may not be eligible or may face a large time-zone gap.
Non-US HQ, so the geography penalty applies.
The AI positioning is thin and comes from press, with no evidence of proprietary AI technology.
The tech stack is not publicly detailed.
greenFlags: Real product with 70+ enterprise clients and recurring revenue growing more than 100% a year (company-reported).
The $13M round is in the preferred range and comes after a shipped product, not before.
Hiring senior engineers: Senior Platform, Data and Full-Stack.
Small team of about 30 with a stated ownership culture and direct access to leadership.
A New York office and US expansion are planned, so US engineering roles may follow.

name: Evvy
evidence: Headline: Evvy raises $40M as it seeks to further women’s health research with vaginal microbiome data
Summary: Women’s health company Evvy announced Tuesday a $40 million Series B led by Catalio Capital Management.

assessment.whatTheyDo: Evvy sells at-home vaginal microbiome tests, run in its own CLIA-certified metagenomic sequencing lab with clinician review, and is building a research dataset and an AI assistant (EvvyAI) on top of results from 100,000+ patients.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Core business is a clinical lab and diagnostics company (sequencing, CLIA/CLEP, clinicians, research). It is not primarily a software company, so engineering may be a supporting function and not the main lever.
The careers page shows no open roles. I found no evidence of senior or staff engineering hiring, so leverage for an engineer is unverified.
EvvyAI is a recent addition. It is not yet clear how much of it is proprietary technology or data versus an LLM layer on top of test results.
Health and lab regulation (CLIA, clinical review, reimbursement) can slow product iteration.
Team size is unknown. After a $60M+ raise and 100,000+ patients, it may already be past the small, high-leverage stage.
Only a weak match to most of the profile's top themes (agent frameworks, databases and distributed systems, dev tools, infrastructure).
assessment.rationale: Evvy is a real, revenue-generating company with technically credible founders, a proprietary dataset and peer-reviewed research, and its size ($40M Series B) fits the preferred round range. However, it is mainly a consumer diagnostics and lab business, so its overlap with this person's core engineering interests is partial. There is also no visible engineering hiring, and it is not clear how much room an engineer would have to shape the product.
assessment.summary: Evvy is a New York-based women's health company founded in 2021 by Priyanka Jain, Laine Bruzek and Pita Navarro. It sells at-home vaginal microbiome sequencing tests with clinician review, and says it has served 100,000+ patients and 3,000 practitioners. It raised a $40M Series B led by Catalio Capital in September 2026 to expand into fertility research and to build out its data and AI tools. It is a real product with proprietary data, but a diagnostics and lab company first, so it fits an engineer-joiner only partially.
assessment.product: At-home vaginal swab kits that are mailed to Evvy's lab and analysed with metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS). Results go to a patient portal with clinical interpretation and treatment recommendations. It also has a practitioner channel, the EvvyAI assistant, and a research program (fertility, preterm birth, IVF outcomes, gynecological cancer). It sells to consumers and to clinicians.
assessment.team: Co-founders Priyanka Jain (CEO; previously head of product at AI hiring startup pymetrics for four years), Laine Bruzek (consumer design) and Pita Navarro (molecular biology). Press describes the team as including OB/GYNs and vaginal microbiome researchers from UCSF, Stanford, Harvard and Cleveland Clinic. I did not find the total headcount.
assessment.funding: $60M+ raised in total. Series A: $14M in September 2023, led by Left Lane Capital. Series B: $40M in September 2026, led by Catalio Capital Management. Other named investors include General Catalyst, US Fertility and Labcorp Venture Fund.
redFlags: No open roles listed on the careers page, so engineering hiring is unconfirmed.
Engineering is likely a supporting function within a lab and clinical business.
The AI layer's differentiation is unverified.
greenFlags: Real, shipped product with 100,000+ patients and 3,000 practitioners.
Proprietary longitudinal microbiome dataset plus lab operations, which is more of a moat than a GPT wrapper.
15 peer-reviewed publications and abstracts, including novel BV subtypes and hundreds of new microbiome genomes.
Founders combine product/AI, design and molecular biology backgrounds.
$40M round is within the preferred range and follows a $14M Series A, so it is not a huge seed with no product.
NYC-based (a preferred state) and open to remote for the right candidate.

name: Exein
evidence: Headline: Exein raises $270m to fight AI hackers, doubles valuation

assessment.whatTheyDo: Exein builds embedded and runtime security for connected devices and 'Physical AI' (robots, vehicles, industrial and medical machines), including a kernel-level eBPF runtime agent, a firmware analyzer and a processor-level security layer.
concerns: Headquartered in Rome, Italy, so it is harder to join from the US. The only engineering role found is Remote (EMEA), and the only other role is in Rome. The US presence is a planned Bay Area office and not yet an established engineering hub.

A $270M Series C at a $1.7B valuation (over $600M raised in total) means a much larger, later-stage company than the 'small team, high-leverage' profile. The round is well above the $2M–$150M preferred range.
Its core market is embedded and IoT security sold to device makers, which is outside the person's top interests (consumer, vertical AI, agent tooling, databases and infrastructure, SaaS).
'Physical AI' is a hype-adjacent framing. The underlying technology looks like established embedded Linux security, though the ARR growth suggests real traction.
Team size is not disclosed, and the careers page lists only two roles: an Executive Assistant and a Linux Security Engineer. No senior or staff US engineering roles were found.
Most of the figures come from Exein's own press release and syndicated coverage (2B devices, ARR up 4x). I could not verify them independently.
assessment.rationale: Exein is a real, technically substantive security company with a technical founder, revenue traction and a credible investor base. It scores modestly because it is Rome-based with EMEA-only remote hiring, it is now a late-stage unicorn rather than a small high-leverage team, and its niche is embedded security, which is only a mid-weight interest. A US-based engineer would have little to apply to today, so the geography penalty is significant.
assessment.summary: Exein is a Rome-founded (2018) embedded and runtime cybersecurity company led by CEO Gianni Cuozzo. It just raised a $270M Series C at a $1.7B valuation, led by Headline, and says its software runs on roughly 2B devices. It is a legitimate, growing company, but it is late-stage and Europe-centric, with only a small number of open roles and a US office still being set up.
assessment.product: Exein Runtime and Photon, a kernel-level (eBPF-based) runtime protection agent for Linux devices, and Exein Analyzer, a firmware and software analysis tool. They are sold to device and OEM manufacturers in industrial, automotive, medical, energy, semiconductor and robotics. The company positions them as a security layer for 'Physical AI'.
assessment.team: Founder and CEO Gianni Cuozzo, who is Italian-German, grew up in Darmstadt, Germany, and moved into cybersecurity after starting in economics. I could not verify his deeper technical background or the rest of the leadership. Offices are in Rome, Germany, Taiwan and the US, and the US office is being built out in the Bay Area. Headcount is not disclosed.
assessment.funding: $270M Series C around 2026-09-15 at a $1.7B valuation, more than $600M raised in total. Led by Headline, with Sofina, Goldman Sachs, EIB Group (via ETCI), KfW Capital and T.Capital, plus existing backers Balderton and HV Capital. The valuation is reported to have risen about 30x in two years, and H1 2026 ARR is reported at 4x the prior year.
openRoles: Executive Assistant to the CTO (Rome, Italy)
redFlags: Very large late-stage round, and the valuation has risen quickly.
Hiring is EMEA-centric, with no US engineering roles found.
'Physical AI' positioning could be hype.
greenFlags: Technical, founder-led company operating since 2018 with a shipped product.
Reported 4x ARR growth in H1 2026 and deployment on about 2B devices, per the company.
Real kernel-level (eBPF) engineering work.
A Bay Area office is planned, so US engineering roles may open.

name: Integral
evidence: Headline: Integral lands €18M Series A for AI-native accounting and tax services

Summary: Berlin-based accounting technologycompany Integral has raised €18 million in a Series A round to expand itsAI-powered accounting, tax and payroll services for small and medium-sizedbusinesses. The rou...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Berlin-based AI-native accounting, tax and payroll services firm for German SMEs, where AI agents do the bookkeeping, tax and payroll work and licensed professionals at an affiliated tax firm (Integral Tax) review and sign off.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
Agent frameworks, evaluation, and LLM tooling
concerns: Headquartered in Berlin and focused on the German market (German tax and accounting law). Joining from the US means visa and relocation, or a permanent time-zone gap. This is a material penalty.
The business is a services firm rather than pure software. Margins and scaling depend on licensed professionals, and Integral Tax is a separate affiliated entity.
Roles are listed under Integral Services GmbH in Berlin. I found no evidence of remote or US hiring.
Series A investors are strong, but the team size and product details are not public. I could not confirm how close engineers are to product decisions.
Regulatory constraints in German tax and audit work (professional licensing, liability) could limit how far the automation can go.
assessment.rationale: It fits the applied-AI-in-finance theme well. The technical co-founder (CTO) and a CEO with a Penta/Qonto track record are credible, and the company reports that agents already prepare bookkeeping end-to-end for over half of clients. The Berlin location, German-only market and services-heavy model pull the score down for a US-based candidate.
assessment.summary: Integral was founded in 2024 by Lukas Zörner (CEO, co-founder of Penta, then at Qonto Germany) and Anil Can Baykal (CTO). It raised a €18M Series A in September 2026 co-led by Mosaic Ventures and Reid Hoffman, bringing total funding to over €30M. It builds an agent-driven accounting, tax and payroll operation for German SMEs, with licensed professionals taking legal responsibility. The thesis is real and the product is in production, but the location and services-heavy model limit fit for a US-based engineer.
assessment.product: An AI agent platform that reconciles invoices and bank transactions, creates account postings, and prepares payroll runs and tax filings for German SMEs. Licensed professionals at the affiliated Integral Tax firm review exceptions and approve filings, and their reviews feed back into the system. The company says agents now prepare bookkeeping end-to-end for more than half of clients, monthly turnaround has gone from weeks to hours, and each professional serves roughly twice as many clients as at the start of 2026.
assessment.team: Lukas Zörner (CEO) co-founded Penta, which grew to about 50,000 customers, then ran Qonto's German operations after Qonto acquired Penta in 2022. Anil Can Baykal is co-founder and CTO; I did not verify his background. Total team size is not published. The company says it combines licensed tax professionals and AI engineers.
assessment.funding: €18M Series A (September 2026), co-led by Mosaic Ventures and Reid Hoffman. Existing investors Cherry Ventures, General Catalyst and Puzzle Ventures increased their stakes. An earlier €6.3M round was reported in February 2025, and a further round in November 2025. Total funding exceeds €30M.
redFlags: Berlin-only hiring evidence and a German-market focus make this hard for a US-based candidate.

assessment.whatTheyDo: Fabless semiconductor company designing standard-CMOS Ka-band beamformer chips (ConnectKa) for electronically steerable satellite user-terminal antennas.
concerns: Headquartered in Antwerp, Belgium. All six open roles are on-site in Antwerp, with no sign of remote or US hiring. Joining from the US would need a visa and relocation.
This is analog/RF/mmWave IC design, not software. A software engineer and PM would have little leverage or relevant work here. The open roles are RF, antenna, supply chain and product engineering.
It matches none of the person's top-weighted themes: consumer apps, applied AI, agent tooling, databases and infrastructure, or SaaS.

The market is tied to satellite terminals and LEO/MEO constellation build-outs, which are capital-intensive and depend on a few large customers. The company website mentions only 2 pilot customers as of Feb 2026.
The company is moving from prototype to mass production, which carries semiconductor execution risks: foundry, yield and supply chain. It is hiring a Director of Supply Chain.
assessment.rationale: TUSK IC is a real, technically deep, KU Leuven-derived hardware company with an ESA contract and a €15M Series A. It is a poor fit for a US-based software/PM candidate: the work is RF IC design, the roles are on-site in Belgium, and it touches only the low-weight hardware theme. The score is capped by the foreign-HQ penalty and the mismatch in discipline.
assessment.summary: TUSK IC is an Antwerp fabless mmWave IC company, spun out of KU Leuven in 2018. It builds standard-CMOS Ka-band beamformer chips for flat-panel satellite antennas. It just closed a €15M Series A led by Matterwave Ventures, FORWARD.one and the Flanders Future Tech Fund to move from prototype to volume production. It is a credible deep-tech company, but it is a hardware/RF business in Belgium, so it is largely irrelevant to a US-based software/product person.
assessment.product: ConnectKa: transmit/receive beamformer chips and low-noise amplifiers built in mainstream CMOS rather than SiGe. They target electronically steerable flat-panel antennas for LEO/MEO satellite user terminals, and are pitched as lower cost and lower power. Customers are satellite terminal and antenna makers.
assessment.team: Founded in 2018 by four electrical engineers with PhDs from KU Leuven's ESAT-MICAS mmWave research group. Board: Kris Beyen (Chair), Raf Moons, Patrick Reynaert, Wouter Steyaert. Headcount is not published. One search summary named Wouter Steyaert as CEO, but the company's own site lists him as a board member and Kathleen Philips as CEO.
